title: Use GITCREDS_PAT_* as the canonical cache env var name
description:
Builds on #77, which put the compatibility paths in already, so this only moves the write
target and the docs. Revertible on its own.

`GITHUB_PAT_GITLAB_COM`, for a GitLab host, is misleading enough to be a support burden. Legacy
names are still read. A warning fires once per session when a legacy name is what supplied the
credential, and never when the new name is set. It is hand-rolled with base `warning()` and a flag
in the `local()` environment, since `test-standalone.R` requires base only.

On the spelling: #56 suggests `GIT_PAT_`, but `GIT_*` is git's own namespace (`GIT_DIR`,
`GIT_ASKPASS`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT`). Nothing collides today, and `GITCREDS_PAT_*` belongs to the
package that owns it. 

#72 from @melissavanbussel proposed this rename in September 2025.
The one-line change here is the same change. What this PR adds is the compatibility
layer in #77 and the warning, which is why it is a separate branch rather than a review comment.
If you would rather take #72 rebased onto #77, close this one. The flip commit carries a
`Co-authored-by` trailer either way.

Anyone vendoring `git-auth.R` will want to re-vendor. An older copy computes the legacy name, so
its cache no longer shares a slot with this one. Tracked in r-lib/pkgdepends#484.

Closes #56

title: Accept GITCREDS_PAT_* alongside GITHUB_PAT_*
description:
Groundwork for the rename in #56, with no behavior change. Reads accept either name, new one
first. Writes still go to `GITHUB_PAT_*`, and `gitcreds_cache_envvar()` still returns the legacy
name, so nothing moves for existing users. Early adopters can start setting the new name now.

Two details worth a look.

The `FAIL` sentinel is only honored under the canonical name. A vendored older copy of
`git-auth.R` writes `FAIL` to the legacy name (pkgdepends does this in `git_creds_for_url()`), and
honoring that through the fallback would let one package suppress a credential that is present.
Reprex in r-lib/pkgdepends#484.

`gitcreds_delete_cache()` now unsets both names. With a fallback in place, unsetting only one
leaves a stale legacy value that the fallback then returns, so `gitcreds_set()` would look like it
ignored a rotated token.

Also widens the `^GITHUB_PAT` scrub in `tests/testthat/helper.R`, so tests stay isolated from the
developer's own environment.

Refs #56

title: Name the URL and cache env var in the no-credentials error
description:
The `gitcreds_no_credentials` condition already carries `url`, but the message doesn't use it:

```
Error: Could not find any credentials
```

So a user who needs to set the environment variable has no way to learn its name at the moment
they need it. That is the confusion reported in #56. Proposed message:

```
Error: Could not find any credentials for 'https://codeberg.org'.
Run `gitcreds_set("https://codeberg.org")`, or set the
`GITHUB_PAT_CODEBERG_ORG` environment variable.
```

No behavior change and no new dependency. This is independent of the rename discussed in #56 and
worth having whichever way that goes.

Refs #56

title: Change GITHUB_PAT_ prefix to more generic GIT_PAT_
description:
Change GITHUB_PAT_ prefix to more generic GIT_PAT_ to remove confusion for non-GitHub users

Fixes #56

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to gitcreds website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the gitcreds website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: Replace mockery
description:
Closes #57

This PR is part of the tidyverse developer day. It removes mockery as a dependency but turned out quite messy. Feel free to close it. No hurt feelings :-)

In particular here are potential problems I see:

* The tests may not expose some problems. Many tests are called via a wrapper to `test_that()` which I didn't fully understand. Some tests seem to fail interactively but don't fail when calling `test()`.
* In R/git-auth.R I messed up the order in which the functions are defined, sorry :-(. 
* `local()` still has some functions. If `local()` was necessary to support mockery, then removing mockery should result in extracting all functions out of `local()` but that's not the case.
* R CMD check and test coverage fail on GitHub Actions for Windows and MacOS.

title: Better git error messages, include stderr
Fix older git versions on Windows
description:
The issue is that system2() uses writeLines()
to write out the standard input to a file, and this
uses \r\n EOLs on Windows. Older git versions
or git for Windows installers (before 2.25.1) do not
handle \r\n as EOL when dealing with credentials.
